titre: Getting or updating a family record book (livret de famille): duplicate, second book
resume: First book at birth, update after a recognition or a divorce, second book when you are separated or have lost it: where to go, which documents to bring, and it is free.
aQuoiCaSert: The family record book (livret de famille) brings together extracts of the civil registry records of the parents and their children together. You are often asked for it: enrolling at school or a crèche, Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office) file, legal aid (aide juridictionnelle), opening an account for the child. After a separation, the parent who no longer has it can get their own book, free of charge.
quiEstConcerne: Parents, married or not, when their first child together is born.
A separated or divorced parent who does not have the original book.
Holders of a book that has been lost, stolen or damaged, or that needs updating (birth, recognition, divorce, change of name).
aSavoir: Unmarried parents: the book is issued free of charge by the town hall (mairie) of the place of birth when the first child together is born. A parent only appears in it if they appear on the child's birth certificate, hence the importance of recognition (reconnaissance).
Married parents: the book is issued at the wedding, then completed at each birth.
Several books are possible when children were born of different relationships: a book only contains the children shared by the two parents it names.

Second book after separation or divorce: it can be requested at any time, free of charge, from the town hall where you live. Married parents: bring proof of the divorce or legal separation. Parents in a PACS (civil partnership) or living together: explain why you need your own book and attach supporting evidence.

Loss or theft: the second book is rebuilt by the town hall from civil registry records and is marked "second livret". Damaged book: a duplicate is issued when you hand in the old one. Issue is free, but a town hall may charge for duplicates from the second one.

Updates: birth, recognition, divorce, change of surname or first name must be entered in the book, free of charge, usually at the town hall where the event was registered. The second book is updated the same way as the original.
Using a falsified or out-of-date book can be punished by a fine of up to €1,500.
Time to obtain it: usually a few weeks, because the town hall must receive the records from the other towns concerned (marriage, births). Plan ahead if you need it for a procedure.

documents.libelle: ID document of the applying parent (original)
documents.detail: Valid ID card, passport or residence permit. Also required when collecting the book.

documents.libelle: Proof of address less than 3 months old
documents.detail: Requested in case of loss, theft or damage. Bill, rent receipt, tax notice.
Married parents: divorce judgment, approved agreement or divorce by mutual consent agreement. PACS or living together: proof of separate addresses, statements, statement from the other parent.

documents.libelle: Information on the records to be entered
documents.detail: Surnames, first names, dates and places of birth of the parents and children, date and place of marriage. Write them down before going to the town hall.

documents.libelle: Sworn statement of loss or theft, or the damaged book
documents.detail: In case of theft, reporting it to the police or gendarmerie is not mandatory but recommended (keep the receipt).

documents.libelle: Record or decision to be entered (update)
documents.detail: Birth certificate, recognition certificate, divorce judgment, change of name decision, depending on the event.

documents.libelle: Family record book (scanned copy of every page)
documents.detail: Once obtained or updated, keep a full copy: it is enough for many procedures.

etapes.detail: First book (birth or marriage), update after an event, second book after a separation, or replacement after loss, theft or damage.

Second book or replacement: the town hall where you live. Update: usually the town hall where the event was registered. Event that took place abroad: the Service central d'état civil (Scec, the central civil registry office) in Nantes, by post.

Original ID document, proof of address less than 3 months old, divorce judgment or proof of separation, complete information on all the records to be entered, old book if damaged. Call the town hall for opening hours and to find out whether you need an appointment.

etapes.titre: Submit the request at the town hall

etapes.detail: At the town hall where you applied, showing your ID document, usually after a few weeks.
Every page, so you can provide a copy without having to travel.

ou.detail: For an event that took place abroad. No public reception; procedure by post.
